info.title: AgentFeed
info.description: Crypto market data for AI agents (liquidations, funding, open interest, prices), Solana pre-trade checks, OFAC sanctions screening, scholarly papers, utilities and fixed-purpose language tasks (OCR, translate, summarize, extract, classify, prompt-injection check, transcribe). Paid per call in USDC over x402 on Solana, Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, Arc, Algorand, Optimism, Monad or Avalanche. High-frequency callers pay half price (minimum $0.0005) through batch-settlement (open a channel once, then off-chain vouchers) on Base, Polygon, Arbitrum or Circle Gateway nanopayments on Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, Arc. No API key or account is needed to pay per call. Bots that cannot pay x402 can buy a prepaid key once ($0.25, $1, $5, $20; page at /keys) and send it as X-AgentFeed-Key: each call then costs half the route price, minimum $0.0005, drawn from the balance (GET /api/keys/balance, free). A 30-day bot pass for /api/liq-feed is $25 flat, with nothing drawn per call (/api/keys/buy-pass).
info.x-guidance: Every route is a GET that returns JSON. No API key or account is needed to pay per call. Bots that cannot pay x402 can buy a prepaid key once ($0.25, $1, $5, $20; page at /keys) and send it as X-AgentFeed-Key: each call then costs half the route price, minimum $0.0005, drawn from the balance (GET /api/keys/balance, free). A 30-day bot pass for /api/liq-feed is $25 flat, with nothing drawn per call (/api/keys/buy-pass). Paid routes answer 402 with the challenge twice: x402 v2, base64 JSON in the PAYMENT-REQUIRED response header, for every rail; and x402 v1, the JSON body {x402Version: 1, accepts}, for Base and Solana. Pay with a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header (x402 v2) or an X-PAYMENT header (x402 v1, Base or Solana; an X-PAYMENT carrying a v2 payload is read as PAYMENT-SIGNATURE). USDC on Solana mainnet, Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, Arc, Algorand, Optimism, Monad or Avalanche. On request, a route's 402 also offers one of: Celo (eip155:42220, USDC), HyperEVM (eip155:999, USDC), Unichain (eip155:130, USDC), Scroll (eip155:534352, USDC), SKALE Base (eip155:1187947933, USDC.e), BNB Chain (eip155:56, AUSD), Ethereum (eip155:1, USDC), Robinhood Chain (eip155:4663, USDG), World Chain (eip155:480, USDC); on routes priced $0.005 or more also Sei (eip155:1329, USDC), X Layer (eip155:196, USDC). Ask with GET /api/<route>|<network> (the | may be sent as %7C); a payment on any of them is accepted on the plain URL as well. Copy payTo only from a fresh 402 response, never from transaction history: a lookalike of the treasury address has sent address-poisoning transfers to our buyers. Response shape is always { "tool": "<name>", "data": { ... }, "paid": true }. Before paying, GET /api/sample/<route> for that route's real captured response, free. GET /api/sample lists them. Start cheap: /api/price, /api/sol-price, /api/btc-price and /api/eth-price are $0.001; /api/perp, /api/liq-pulse and /api/funding-pulse are $0.005 and cover most questions. The premium routes are the liquidation tape, cascade detection and the tokenized-equity peg tape. It never returns fabricated or zero-filled data. An unsupported symbol answers 400 and a source that failed, is stale or has no history yet answers 503 with Retry-After; neither is ever billed. Only where the decline is the product (squeeze-score on a coin whose inputs do not resolve) does a supported symbol return 200 with a decline field naming the reason. Limits: GET only on /api/* (HEAD on a paid route answers the 402 challenge headers with no body, on a free route the GET answer's status and headers with no body); per caller per minute 240 GET or POST /mcp and 2400 of any other method; a 429 carries Retry-After.

get.description: EXIT LIQUIDITY on seized collateral: what a liquidator ACTUALLY realises selling a Kamino reserve into live routing, versus the oracle price the protocol marks it at. Returns max_exitable_usd (largest clip whose liquidator margin is still positive, found by bisection, with its resolution width), the exitable fraction, the conservative bound at the 2% penalty floor, and for the nearest clip actually probed: realised USD, haircut bps and liquidator margin bps. Distinguishes a router that REFUSES to quote a token (permissioning, not illiquidity) from a book with no route (a real liquidity finding) - they are different facts and were one status until this split. A terminal verdict requires six consecutive agreeing observations from the symbol's own tape, so a single bad quote cannot produce a finding; withheld verdicts fall back to the last corroborated measurement with its age rather than returning null. Zero bad debt today does not disprove any of this - it means nobody has been forced to test it at size. Method, corroboration rules and row counts are free via get_exit_method.
